source.title: CodeMMLU: A Multi-Task Benchmark for Assessing Code Understanding Capabilities of CodeLLMs
source.authors: Dung Nguyen Manh; Thang Phan Chau; Nam Le Hai; Thong T. Doan; Nam V. Nguyen; Quang Pham; N. Bui

record.tranche_reason: The paper compares downstream CodeMMLU performance across model sizes and families, bearing on downstream predictability with a benchmark accuracy measure rather than pretraining loss.
record.gate_note: The paper reports model evaluations and its own conclusion that scaling by size holds partially within a family but not across families. Results on prompting, answer-order bias, benchmark correlations, and leakage do not test the listed scaling versions and are not scaling rows.
record.test_reason: This is a code-understanding benchmark paper. Its own accuracy results for 40+ models of different sizes, including several within-family size series (CodeLlama 7/13/34B, Llama3 8/70B, Qwen2 0.5–57B, DSCoder 6.7/33B), bear on whether downstream performance rises with scale (V6) in a new setting: code MCQ. Scaling is incidental, not controlled, and no curve is fitted.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors say size scaling holds partially within a family but not across families, stressing pre-training, post-training and architecture. In Section 4.2 they also stress data quality and instruction tuning. They note knowledge tasks follow scaling more closely than real-world tasks. Scaling is a side finding; the paper's main conclusions are about the benchmark, MCQ bias, and CoT hurting performance.
record.recipe_differences: Uses benchmark accuracy on CodeMMLU across independently developed models; it does not measure held-out pretraining loss or run controlled scaling sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported size-performance pattern differs within versus across model families; the authors also identify pre-training, post-training, and architecture as relevant factors.

fits_no_version.finding: Knowledge-test accuracy correlates moderately with fundamental-task accuracy across 43 LLMs (r=0.61).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Performance on code-knowledge MCQ is associated with performance on code-skill tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: Instruction tuning raises CodeMMLU accuracy substantially, e.g. about 29% for DeepSeek-Coder-33B over its base.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-training changes downstream code performance at fixed size.

record.problems: The scaling discussion is based on comparisons among independently developed models rather than controlled training runs. Model family, training stage, pre-training data, post-training, and architecture can vary alongside parameter count; the paper does not fit scaling curves or report uncertainty for the scaling comparison.
record.rows_left_out: Per-model task accuracy results in Tables 3, 9, 10, and 11 were not extracted as individual scaling rows: the paper's relevant scaling result is stated as an aggregate within-family/across-family finding, and the tables do not provide a controlled scaling sweep or fitted curve.

untested.parts: Pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute: not measured.
No other modalities or training regimes.
Predictability from pretraining loss, any fitted trend, and controlled same-recipe size sweeps.
No exponent fitting or fit-choice analysis.

missing.what: Per-model within-family accuracies by size, including the reversals noted above
Task-type split: knowledge tasks follow scaling, fundamental or real-world tasks do not

record.verdict_notes: The record's tranche T2 was changed to T3, since this is a new downstream setting with incidental scaling results. The across-family label was downgraded from challenges to limits_scope: cross-family comparisons confound data and training, which V6 does not claim to be controlled. Evidence is uncontrolled and has no uncertainty estimates.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining cross-entropy as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
Fitting power laws on small runs and predicting substantially larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Controlled comparisons of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Power-law behavior in other modalities, repeated-data training, fine-tuning, or transfer.
The paper evaluates CodeMMLU accuracy across model sizes/families, but does not test predictability from pretraining loss or on downstream tasks beyond this benchmark.
Fitted exponents, compute-optimal splits, fitting-method sensitivity, and curve bending.

rows.subject: CodeMMLU evaluations across models within the same model family
rows.size_stated: parameters ranging from 1 billion to over 70 billion across the evaluated models
rows.stage_stated: base and instructed/chat versions were included
rows.operation_detail: Compared CodeMMLU accuracy across model sizes within model families.
rows.value: Scaling laws tied to model size hold partially within the same model family.
rows.note: The paper gives this aggregate characterization rather than a fitted scaling curve or a numerical effect size for the within-family comparisons.
rows.check: The value is only the authors' summary. The tables give within-family numbers, including reversals. In Table 7, DSCoder 7B Instruct (41.59) beats DSCoder 33B Instruct (37.45). Qwen2 7B Instruct (51.86) beats Qwen2 57B-A14B Instruct (47.34). Llama3.1 70B Instruct (59.68) slightly beats 405B Instruct (58.23, Table 3). Training stage and version are confounded with size.

rows.subject: CodeMMLU evaluations across models from different model families
rows.size_stated: parameters ranging from 1 billion to over 70 billion across the evaluated models
rows.stage_stated: base and instructed/chat versions were included
rows.operation_detail: Compared CodeMMLU accuracy across model sizes and model families.
rows.value: Scaling laws tied to model size do not hold across families.
rows.note: The authors attribute cross-family differences to factors including pre-training, post-training, and model architecture.
rows.check: State is right per the authors' words. But families differ in data and training, so this comparison is not the single-recipe scale series V6 describes. The authors attribute the gap to data quality: newer small models match older larger ones. Treat it as a scope condition, not a direct failure of V6.

relationships.reason: The authors say size scaling holds only partially (r1). Tables 3 and 7 show larger family members sometimes scoring lower, e.g. DSCoder 33B vs 7B and Qwen2 57B vs 7B.
relationships.display_finding: Larger family members sometimes scored lower, including DSCoder 33B versus 7B and Qwen2 57B versus 7B.

relationships.condition: across model families with differing data and training
relationships.reason: Size does not predict rank across families (r2); the authors attribute this to data quality and post-training. This qualifies size-only predictability, not same-recipe scaling.
relationships.display_finding: Parameter size failed to predict model rankings, which the authors attributed to data quality and post-training differences.

relationships.condition: knowledge tasks vs fundamental coding tasks
relationships.reason: Based on text, not rows: the Figure 4 caption says knowledge tasks follow scaling while real-world tasks do not. Depends on task type.
relationships.display_finding: Knowledge tasks improved with scale, while real-world tasks did not.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
